original_question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for the mucopolysaccharidosis caused by a deficiency of β-glucuronidase, resulting in abnormal glycosaminoglycan accumulation?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for the mucopolysaccharidosis caused by a deficiency of β-glucuronidase, resulting in abnormal glycosaminoglycan accumulation?
final_qi.long_answer: Mucopolysaccharidosis type VII (Sly syndrome) is due to deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme β-glucuronidase, encoded by the GUSB gene. The GUSB gene is located on chromosome 7 (region 7q11.21), so the responsible mutation resides on chromosome 7.

0.question: Which gene is responsible for the mucopolysaccharidosis caused by a deficiency of β-glucuronidase?

final_answer.long_answer: β-Glucuronidase deficiency (mucopolysaccharidosis type VII, Sly syndrome) is caused by mutations in the GUSB gene, which is mapped to chromosome 7 (region 7q11.21-q11.22). Loss of GUSB activity impairs degradation of glycosaminoglycans, leading to their pathological accumulation characteristic of this mucopolysaccharidosis.
